newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Japanese trader bids mogas up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Japanese trader bids mogas up.

text.p: Singapore gasoline firmed on Friday with crude and higher bids from a Japanese trader, traders said.
A Japanese trader raised his bid for 92-octane unleaded barrels lifting fob Singapore end June to early July to $23.90 per barrel from $23.60 on Thursday.
Some traders said the trader's buying interest was on the back of Indonesian gasoline imports during two refinery shutdowns in July and August.
By market close, state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) had yet to award its second tender to buy June supplies of 87-octane leaded gasoline, a source close to IOC said.
"The tender has not been awarded, it will only be awarded in two hours' time," the source said at 1050GMT.
Market sources had earlier rumoured the 25,000 tonne cargo had been awarded to a Dutch trader at $38 per tonne over Mideast naphtha quotes c+f west coast India.
The tender which sought the June 26-30 cargo, closed June 11 and was valid for a day.
IOC had sought the second June cargo due to a product shortfall caused by the five-day emergency shutdown on June 2 of the 150,000 barrels-per-day state refiner Cochin refinery.
The rumoured price is lower than IOC's first purchase in June at $43 per tonne over Mideast naphtha quotes, c+f Bombay on the west coast June 18-22.
It would translate to a 83 cent per barrel premium over Singapore 92-octane unleaded quotes, c+f, compared to the first award which was at an equivalent of a premium of $2.50.
Traders said the difference could be explained by the relative rise in gasoline and fall in naphtha prices.
The gasoline/naphtha spread has widened to around $3.00 per barrel compared to $2.00-$2.50 a week ago, traders said.
"Gasoline is balanced.. but the market is far from tight, there are barrels," said a trader.
But Mideast cargoes have been diverted west, and fresh Thai cargoes had yet to emerge on the market for July.
Chinese refiners were however heard offering 92-octane unleaded cargoes at $2.00-$2.50 per barrel over Singapore naphtha spot quotes - considered high by the market.
"We will have to wait for Taiwan next week," a trader said on Taiwan's import tender for 95-octane unleaded reformate for July 24-August 15 delivery, closing June 17 and valid for two days.
Naphtha traders confirmed the sale of a 240,000 barrel cargo of light naphtha fob Singapore lifting July from a U.S. major to a Japanese trader, but said details were p+c.
Traders said the level was around 70 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, fob, higher than earlier assessments of 40-50 cents.
"It is still at 40-50 cents... at most," said a Japanese trader. "The market is still in contago."
But firmer prices in the west have starved off sellers offering naphtha cargoes into Asia.
"Nobody is offering...nobody wants to take the risk," said a trader with a major oil company.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
